answer: Resist Sybils by binding each identity to one exclusive message inlet that only its key can answer. The protocol plants an orchard of unpredictable liveness probes: each probe is delivered only to that inlet and must be signed within seconds, or a locked deposit is slashed and earnings freeze. A farm cannot share one inbox across puppets, because inlets are unique per key and probes arrive like a comet—sudden, brief, and useless if answered late. Running N identities therefore costs N always-on endpoints plus N at-risk deposits.
